insights.title: Rain does not cover crop water needs
insights.body: On average, crops here need about 568 mm more water each year than rain provides. Irrigation or drought-tolerant crops matter.

insights.title: Fields are greenest in July, barest in April
insights.body: Satellite greenness of the farmland here peaks at 0.68 and drops to 0.43 (0 = bare, 1 = dense crop). The low months are when soil is most exposed to rain and wind.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rice, Salt-tolerant rice and Sugarcane score highest on climate, water and soil fit.
insights.source: Sowcast crop-fit score using measured climate and soil

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 868 mm
consequences.detail: That is 24% below the 1,140 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: No clear long-term change since 2001
consequences.detail: Rain, heat and dry spells show no reliable trend here. The bigger risk is the swing from one year to the next.
consequences.action: Plan for a bad year rather than a changing average.
